excerpt: Note that unlike system cards, Risk Reports will not be published with each new model release.
paraphrase: Risk Reports differ from system cards in that they are not tied to each new model release.

excerpt: Separate from our publication of Risk Reports, we will publish an analysis of an individual model’s relevant risks (e.g., how the model’s capabilities and propensities affect or change prior analyses) in the following circumstances:
paraphrase: In addition to periodic Risk Reports, Anthropic will publish individual model risk analyses under specified circumstances.

context_stem: We will publish an analysis of an individual model's relevant risks in the following circumstances:
excerpt: When we publicly deploy a model that we determine is (1) significantly more capable than (2) all models for which we have publicly analyzed risks related to chemical/biological weapons production, high-stakes misalignment, or automated R&D (e.g., in a prior Risk Report, System Card, or other public artifact).
paraphrase: An off-cycle analysis is published when a publicly deployed model is judged significantly more capable than all previously publicly risk-assessed models on key threat domains.
stated_bar: significantly more capable than all models for which we have publicly analyzed risks

context_stem: We will publish an analysis of an individual model's relevant risks in the following circumstances:
excerpt: Within 30 days of determining that we have an internally deployed model that (1) could pose risks related to high-stakes misalignment or automated R&D that (2) significantly exceed those of all models for which we have publicly analyzed such risks (e.g., in a prior Risk Report, System Card, or other public artifact).
paraphrase: An off-cycle analysis is published within 30 days of determining an internal model poses materially greater misalignment or automated R&D risk than all previously publicly assessed models.
stated_bar: within 30 days; significantly exceed those of all models for which we have publicly analyzed such risks

excerpt: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
paraphrase: A set of principles governs Anthropic's approach to Risk Reports.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We intend for our Risk Reports to be direct, candid, and informative about how we see the risks of our systems and our state of preparedness for them.
paraphrase: Anthropic aims for Risk Reports to be direct, candid, and informative about risks and preparedness.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: In particular, we will acknowledge when we view certain models as posing significant risks in absolute terms, even if our marginal contribution to overall ecosystem risk may be relatively limited when taking other developers’ AI models into account.
paraphrase: Anthropic will acknowledge absolute risk from its models even when its marginal contribution to ecosystem-wide risk seems limited.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We will put significant effort into investigating (for example, via capability evaluations) the case for risk, and into sharing what we find.
paraphrase: Anthropic will invest significant effort in investigating and disclosing evidence relevant to risk.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: When a Risk Report describes risk mitigations we have in place (or plan to implement shortly), we will keep our future practices in line with this description or track and report noteworthy changes and deviations (generally via subsequent Risk Reports).
paraphrase: Anthropic will either maintain described mitigation practices or report noteworthy deviations from them in future Risk Reports.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We should make a strong attempt to ensure that ongoing (as opposed to temporary) changes do not significantly increase the level of risk.
paraphrase: Anthropic will strongly attempt to prevent ongoing practice changes from significantly increasing risk.

excerpt: We will describe how we identify, evaluate, and mitigate catastrophic risks.
paraphrase: Anthropic will describe its process for identifying, evaluating, and mitigating catastrophic risks.

excerpt: A Risk Report will document the following:
paraphrase: The Risk Report will document a specified set of items.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following (Factual information):
excerpt: Threat model identification: Our criteria for determining which catastrophic risks (i.e., threat models) we assess.
paraphrase: The report will state the criteria used to determine which catastrophic risks are assessed.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following (Factual information):
excerpt: Threat model specification: The relevant threat models (which will, at a minimum, include those discussed above).
paraphrase: The report will specify the relevant threat models, including at minimum those already discussed.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following (Factual information):
excerpt: Evidence (including evaluations) about relevant model capabilities and behaviors: For each in-scope model, capability and alignment evaluations (conducted internally and by external parties as appropriate), their results, and (as appropriate) other evidence we considered in assessing the level of risk.
paraphrase: For each in-scope model, the report will present capability and alignment evaluations, their results, and other relevant evidence considered.
